State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
M/S Levely Gen. Store vs Harcharan Singh & Anr. on 6 January, 2009
H
 
 
 

 

 

 H.P.
STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, SHIMLA , CAMP AT
MANDI. 

 

 Appeal
No. 266/2005 

 

Date of Decision 06.01.2009. 

 

M/s Levely Gen. Store, Shop No.71 Sankan Garden
Mandi, 

 

Distt. Mandi, HP through its Prop. Harmit Singh. 

 

 ..Appellant. 

 

 Versus 

 

 

 

1. Harcharan Singh S/o Sh. Prit Pal Singh R/o H. No. 95/3 

 

 Jail Road
Mandi, Distt. Mandi, HP., 

 

  

 

2. K. Sons (Nokia Distributor) opposite Post Office
Sector 

 

 1M, Parwanoo, Distt. Solan, HP. 

 

  

 

.Respondents. 

 

Honble Mr.
Justice Arun Kumar Goel, President. 

 

Honble Mrs.
Saroj Sharma, Member.
Whether
Approved for reporting? No. 

 

  

 

For the Appellant. Mr. M.P. Sehgal, Advocate.
For the
Respondent No.1 In person.
O R D E
R:
Justice Arun Kumar Goel (Retd.) President (Oral).
While
arguing in support of this appeal, Mr. Sehgal learned
counsel for the appellant submitted that the complaint was not maintainable as
it was bad for non joinder of necessary parties i.e. the manufacturer of the
mobile set in question. He further
submitted that the phone was not handed over to the appellant pointing out any
defect. Further according to him
District Forum below fell into error by ignoring the limited warranty
conditions and also there being no report of the expert regarding nature and
character of the defect in the mobile handset in question.
2. Admittedly
case of the parties as made out from the complaint file is, that respondent
No.1 purchased Nokia Make Mobile Phone Model 3120 from the appellant for Rs.
5350/- on 3.3.2005. At the time of
hearing it was not disputed that it was under warranty for a period of 1
year. According to respondent No.1 it
stopped functioning due to defects on its screen on the very next day due to
some manufacturing defect and it was brought to the notice of the
appellant. Respondent No.1 further
pleaded that since he was using the mobile phone for the last 4 years, as
such he was well conversant with its functioning. He handed over the handset for replacement with
a new one. Appellant stated that it asked respondent No.2 to replace the same,
but without any consequence, so it returned the handset in question on 9.3.2005
to him in the same condition, thus according to respondent No.1 a defective
phone was supplied to him by the appellant, therefore this being a deficiency
in service, as such complaint was filed.
So far respondent No.2 is concerned, it was set ex parte in the complaint,
and in the present appeal also situation is the same.
3. So far appellant is concerned, it admits having sold the
mobile handset in question. This was
purchased by respondent No.1 after opening the sealed pack and then having used
the same for some time before its purchase. There was no defect at the time of sale. Set having been handed over to the appellant
on 5.3.2005 was denied and the plea in this behalf was false, fabricated. Defect,
if any could have developed due to fall of the mobile set or its mishandling by
respondent No.1. In these circumstances
appellant was not liable for handset defect, as such it is pleaded that there
is no deficiency in service.
4. Before
dealing with the submissions of Mr. Sehgal, it may be
observed that sale of the mobile handset to respondent No.1 is admitted vide
bill copy whereof is there on the complaint file. In addition to this respondent No.1 filed his
own affidavit which has remained uncontroverted as no evidence was filed to
counter the facts detailed in his affidavit by the respondent No.1. In these circumstances and keeping in view
the unchallenged as well as uncontroverted evidence of the respondent No.1, we
see no reason to disagree with the conclusions arrived at by the District Forum below while disposing of the
complaint.
5. Faced
with this situation Mr. Sehgal submitted that so far
his client is concerned, mobile handset was never delivered to him by the
appellant. This plea is being noted
simply to be rejected in the face of the averments made in the complaint
regarding handset having been handed over on 5.3.2008 for removal of defect
which was returned by the appellant to the respondent No.1 on 9.3.2005 in the
defective condition, as such submission of Mr. Sehgal
that set was never delivered to the appellant is based on no evidence.
6. In
our opinion manufactures is not a necessary party reason being that it is
something between the manufacturer and the dealer. So far respondent No.1 is concerned,
it had not dealt with the manufacturer of the mobile handset in question. Appellant is the front man from whom the
handset was purchased, when it has been found to be defective. It was for the appellant to have ensured to
either have got it properly repaired or in the alternative to have got it
replaced. How and in what manner, is his outlook. Thus we are of the view that manufacturer was
neither a necessary nor proper party.
Plea based on limited warranty subject to which handset was sold also
does not advance the case of the appellant.
Reason being that the mobile set has been held to be defective,
and the appellant failed to get it either rectified or to replace it. In these circumstances no benefit can be
derived by the appellant from the limited warranty.
7. Plea
that there was no report of expert regarding mobile handset being defective, at
the risk of repetition it may be observed that affidavit filed by the
respondent No.1 to that effect remained uncontroverted. Why no evidence was filed or at least affidavit
of the proprietor of the appellant, Mr. Sehgal had no
answer. Thus this plea is also devoid of
any merit. Ordered
accordingly.
8. No
other point is urged.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, while upholding the order of
the District Forum below, this appeal is dismissed, leaving the parties to bear
their own costs.
All
interim orders passed from time to time in this appeal shall stand vacated
forthwith.
Office
is directed to send copy of the order free of cost to Mr. M.P.
Sehgal, Advocate, District Courts, Mandi
and in the like manner to both the respondents.
Shimla.
6th
January, 2009. (Justice Arun Kumar Goel) Retd.
